newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to import 1.125 mln tonnes of wheat.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to import 1.125 mln tonnes of wheat.

text.p: Bulgaria will need to import a 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat before next year's crop and a further 53,000 tonnes of bread wheat before this year's crop to cover a consumption gap, Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov said on Tuesday.

Bulgaria will need to import wheat because of the poor harvest expected this year due to a long winter and dry spring, he told a news conference, adding the government hopes to import most of the wheat at the end of the harvest period when international grain prices are lower.

Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year created acute grain shortages earlier this year. This year's yield is seen at two tonnes per hectare, down from previous estimates of three tonnes, he added.

Bulgaria planted 1.2 million hectares of wheat last year and the harvest is estimated at around 2.4 million tonnes, of which some 232,000 must be exported under contracts agreed earlier this year to offset bread shortages.
Annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.

"The country urgently needs an additional 53,000 tonnes of bread wheat to cover the gap until the new crop and we hope that the cabinet will announce a tender for the import of this quantity later this week," Varbanov said.
Bulgaria also needs to import 200,000 tonnes of maize to cover the gap before the new crop. "We will call four tenders, each for 50,000 tonnes of maize", he said.
